name: dimir control

winrate_basis.why: no head-to-head winrate exists for Modern in any source this repo can reach: statistics_matchups returns zero rows for the format, statistics_archetypes carries no winrate field, and this run's own fingerprint records winrate_vs_field as all-zero. Recording a number here would be inventing one.

opponent_gameplan: Thoughtseize and cheap counters into Psychic Frog, Murktide Regent and Kaito, winning a long game on card quality; Orcish Bowmasters punishes our cycling directly.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Prose calls it a long game on card quality, but the pitfalls and stance describe a counter war: Thoughtseize and three counters answer our cascade first, then Murktide Regent closes.

key_cards.why: strips the cascade spell before it is ever cast, which is the cheapest way to answer our plan
one mana with replicate for the cascade trigger itself, the counter our own Dispute cannot outnumber
taxes the cycling we use to set up, so building the payload costs us life and gives them a body
the clock they deploy once our cascade has been answered, closing a game they never had to race

primary_gameplan: Bait the first counter, resolve the second cascade with Dispute backup, and rebuild through Bowmasters by cycling only when we can follow up.
pitfalls: Cycling Street Wraith into Orcish Bowmasters and taking free damage plus an Orc army for nothing.
Casting the cascade spell into four open mana because we hold a Dispute; they have three counters and we have one.
Fetching only nonbasics with three Harbinger of the Seas in their deck.
stance_rationale: Every relevant card they own is blue, so the cheapest counter in the format is the whole plan; nothing else in the fifteen improves a matchup decided by a counter war.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: counters the cascade trigger for one mana with replicate for the second copy
one mana against Shardless Agent, Subtlety and Force of Negation
instant-speed graveyard exile with the cascade trigger on the stack
makes our nonbasics Islands, which cuts the red and green halves of the cascade shell

play_plan.keep: A hand with two lands, a cascade spell and a blue source for Dispute; do not keep pure cyclers.
play_plan.goldfish_for: The turn they tap low for Psychic Frog or Kaito, with Dispute and a cascade spell both castable.
play_plan.watch_for: Two open mana on our turn is Spell Snare plus Dispute, so lead Violent Outburst, not Shardless Agent.
play_plan.posture_why: we need their counters spent before the real cascade.
